newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds head up after steady U.S. rates.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds head up after steady U.S. rates.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Tuesday, helped by the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to hold U.S. interest rates steady.
But traders underlined that the market saw very little activity with most now predicting a gradual climb after recent losses.
"The market is slightly long. Nobody is in a hurry to buy at these levels," said a trader at a local bank.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond was up 1/8 at 95-1/2 while the Par bond rose 1/4 to 74-1/8.
Another trader predicted the market "will come back slowly."
Despite the Federal Reserve's decision to hold rates steady, the Argentine market is likely to continue to focus on U.S. markets, considering their recent volatility.
